title: Shifting the Square Root Graph Horizontally
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = sqrt(x) is to be shifted left 0.81 units. Give an equation for the shifted graph and describe the original and shifted curves.

steps.title: Apply the Leftward Horizontal Shift Rule
steps.explanation: To shift the graph of y = sqrt(x) to the left by 0.81 units, replace x with x + 0.81.
steps.why: A horizontal shift left by c > 0 units replaces x with x + c.

steps.title: Determine the Shifted Domain and Endpoint
steps.explanation: The original graph y = sqrt(x) starts at (0, 0) with domain [0, infinity). The shifted graph starts at (-0.81, 0) with domain [-0.81, infinity) and range [0, infinity).
steps.why: The left endpoint of the square root graph occurs where the radicand equals zero.

steps.title: Find the y-Intercept for Sketching
steps.explanation: Evaluating at x = 0 gives y = sqrt(0.81) = 0.9, so the shifted curve crosses the positive y-axis at (0, 0.9).
steps.why: Since 0.9^2 = 0.81, the principal square root of 0.81 is exactly 0.9.
